frequency_question: How often has full revocation or termination of a recognized accrediting body occurred via federal administrative action over the past four decades?
membership_rule: Includes any formal administrative proceeding by the U.S. Department of Education (or predecessor) targeting the national accrediting authority of a major professional field, excluding voluntary relinquishments.
window: Any timeframe up to 101 days matching the target window.

cases.name: ACICS (Accrediting Council for Independent Colleges and Schools) termination proceedings

provenance_note: claims 40 cases from only 3 named (13.3x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 40 major review cycles named/estimated; believed exhaustive for federal institutional/professional accrediting bodies of comparable scale.
known_gaps: Excludes minor advisory warnings that did not result in formal termination proceedings.
skeleton: Total major review cycles of national accrediting bodies examined by the Department of Education over 30 years (~40 major cycles), yielding full revocations that take effect permanently.
multiplier: 0 revocations resulting in permanent loss of authority within the specific short window out of ~40 reviewed major agency renewals.
validity_reason: Administrative law and the statutory framework governing higher education accreditation change slowly over multi-year legislative cycles.
